transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. It's very nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me today. 

I... well, I hope I'm explaining this properly, and I really don't want to sound silly, but... I've been having this little issue lately. It's honestly a bit embarrassing to talk about, because I know how it might sound. But I've been hearing these... voices, I suppose you would call them. 

They're actually quite clear. It mostly happens when I'm alone in my apartment, or sometimes if I'm walking through the empty rooms at the art museum. It just sounds like... well, like women whispering from right behind the walls. And they tell me which photographs belong in the archive. 

I know that probably sounds terribly strange, doesn't it? I hope it's okay that I'm sharing this with you. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Aside from hearing these voices, have you noticed any significant changes in your mood, such as periods where you feel unusually energetic and impulsive, or periods where you feel persistently sad and lose interest in your daily activities?

Oh, that's a very thoughtful question. I... well, I hope I'm answering this the right way. I don't want to make a fuss over nothing, because I know adjusting to not working anymore is probably tricky for everyone, but... yes, I suppose there have been some changes. 

Actually, most of these months since my retirement have been dominated by these long stretches where I feel incredibly... driven? Almost like I have a special purpose, or like I've been chosen for something. I just find myself completely unable to slow down. I must admit, I do get a little bit irritable during those times, which I feel just awful about, because I really do try my best to be pleasant to everyone. 

But then, even with all that intense energy, I also have these quieter, withdrawn days where I just sort of retreat and keep entirely to myself. 

Is... is that the sort of thing you were asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right details. Please let me know if I'm not making sense.
During those times when you are not feeling that intense, driven energy or the withdrawn sadness, do the voices continue to speak to you, or are they only present when your mood is shifting?

Oh, I see what you're asking. You ask such good questions, Dr. Smith. I... well, I feel a little embarrassed to admit this part, because I really do try to be sensible, but... yes. 

There was actually a period recently, for several weeks, where my mood was quite steady. I wasn't feeling overly energized or... or grand, or anything like that. I was just my usual, quiet self. But... the whispers in the apartment, they didn't stop. 

And, oh dear, I hope this doesn't make me sound terribly paranoid—I really don't want you to think poorly of me—but even when I was feeling perfectly calm and fine, I remained completely convinced that the arts people were... well, monitoring my phone. 

Is... is that helpful? I just want to be sure I'm answering you properly and giving you what you need.

Looking back at the past six months, was there a period of at least two weeks where you experienced those voices or the belief that you were being monitored, while your mood was completely stable and not elevated or depressed?

Oh, yes, Dr. Smith. I... I hope I didn't make things confusing just a moment ago, I really do try to be as clear as possible for you. But yes, to answer your question directly... looking back over these last six months, there was definitely a stretch of several weeks where my mood was just... completely normal. I wasn't feeling energized or grand, or sad either. Just very steady. 

But even during those several weeks, I... well, I still heard the whispering in my apartment. And I was still absolutely certain about the arts people monitoring my phone, even though my mood was perfectly fine otherwise. 

I hope it's alright that I'm repeating myself a little bit. Did I explain that timeline the way you needed me to?

During the times you felt sad and withdrawn, did you lose interest in almost all of your usual activities, or did you find it difficult to get out of bed or handle your daily routine for most of the day?

Well... I don't want to make it sound like I'm completely incapable or anything like that. I really do try to keep things tidy and keep up appearances, I promise. But... yes, I suppose during those quieter times, things do slip a little bit. 

I'll just... well, there are long stretches where I'll just sit at my kitchen table for hours. And my little herb pots, which I usually love tending to, they just dry out. I know I should water them, but I just... don't. And I feel awful admitting this, but I haven't been calling my friends back. Even when they invite me to things I'd normally enjoy, like a concert or a gallery opening, I just... I don't feel much interest at all. I just want to stay put. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound terribly lazy. I really do want to be more active, it's just... hard sometimes. Is that the kind of information you were looking for? I want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
During those times when you felt withdrawn and lost interest in your activities, did those feelings last for at least two weeks at a time?

Oh, I... I suppose so. I really don't want to make a fuss about it, but... yes, when I get like that, it does seem to last for a few weeks at a stretch. Two weeks, maybe a bit more. 

I try my best to shake it off, I really do. I don't want you to think I just give up the moment I feel a little blue. But it just sort of... lingers. I hope it's okay that I let it go on that long before asking for help. Am I giving you the right timeline? I want to make sure I'm being helpful.
During those two-week periods when you felt withdrawn and lost interest, did you also experience a significant change in your appetite or sleep patterns?

Well, I... I don't think so? I mean, I always try to eat a little something, even just a piece of toast or some soup, so I'm not completely skipping meals or anything terrible like that. I don't want you to think I'm not taking care of myself. And my sleep... well, I suppose I might toss and turn a bit, or maybe nap in the afternoon, but I wouldn't say it's a huge, significant change. 

I try to keep to a normal schedule as best I can. I hope that's the right answer... I just haven't really noticed any drastic problems with eating or sleeping during those times. Is that alright?
During those times when you felt that intense, driven energy, did you feel like you needed significantly less sleep than usual, yet still felt completely refreshed and energetic the next day?

Well... yes, I suppose I do sleep a bit less during those energetic times. I don't want to sound like I'm neglecting my health, because I know sleep is important, I really do. But... it's just that I don't seem to need as much of it. 

I might only sleep for, oh, maybe two or three hours? And then I'll wake up before dawn, and I just feel... completely ready to go. I don't feel tired at all. It's almost like... well, I tell myself that sleep is for people who don't have an archive to rescue. There's just so much to do, and I feel so capable of doing it all. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm being reckless with my routine. I just feel so wonderfully refreshed, even with those few hours. Is that... is that normal for the kind of energy you're asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right sort of details.
During those times when you felt that intense, driven energy and needed very little sleep, did those periods last for at least an entire week, or were they shorter than that?

Oh, well... yes, they definitely last for at least a week. I really don't want to sound like I'm completely out of control, but... if I'm being perfectly honest, those bursts—the times with hardly any sleep, all those racing plans, the spending, and just that furious energy—they've actually taken up about six months in total recently. 

I know that sounds like a terribly long time to be so... wound up. I hope you don't think poorly of me for letting it go on like that. I just felt so productive, you know? I really thought I was doing well. Is it alright that I'm telling you it lasted that long? I just want to be as accurate as possible for you.
